system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Region-mass aggregation with support-derived thresholds for robust per-image MVFA scores
SUMMARY: Standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, threshold the fused map at a support-derived level, and score each image by the excess mass of its strongest connected region.
HYPOTHESIS: Region-mass aggregation keeps image AUROC within 1 point of max pooling on clean data and loses at most one third as much AUROC as max pooling when 3 spurious spikes are injected into normal test maps.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: image aggregation (max pixel vs. top-1% mean vs. region mass), with support z-score normalisation in all inductive variants. Region mass: tau_pix = 99th percentile of support LOO fused pixel scores; regions = 8-connected components of {x: m(x) > tau_pix}; mass(R) = sum_{x in R} (m(x) - tau_pix); image score = max_R mass(R) (0 if no region). Dependent variables: image AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, AUROC drop under injection of 1-5 spurious single-patch spikes into normal test maps, per-image score shift under resampling.
RATIONALE: MVFA's image score is the maximum fused pixel, which one spurious pixel can decide. G-Anomaly's view that anomalies are coherent regions suggests aggregating at region level: threshold the fused map at a support-derived level, form connected regions, and score an image by its strongest region's mass (mean excess score times area). Combined with support-standardised branches, this gives a per-image score that is robust to isolated spikes and needs no test-set statistics.
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: support LOO z-scores per branch and level; fused map m = mean; remove test-set min-max. 2) utils.py: region_mass(m, tau) with scipy.ndimage.label (8-connectivity). 3) tau_pix from support LOO fused maps (99th percentile); image threshold tau_img = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores. 4) Stress test: inject k in {1, 3, 5} single-patch spikes (value = 99.9th percentile of the image's map + 3 std) at random positions in normal test maps. Hyper-parameters: percentiles 99 and 95; no training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) support z-score normalisation with max pooling, (ii) top-1% mean, (iii) region mass. Metrics: image AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, AUROC under spike injection, score shift under resampling. Falsified if region mass loses more than 1 point of clean AUROC or does not reduce the injected-spike AUROC drop by at least half.

Idea B:
TITLE: Scan statistic over calibrated log-odds maps with a support-derived null for the image score
SUMMARY: Score each image by the largest summed log-odds over connected candidate regions of its calibrated anomaly map, and convert it to a p-value with the null distribution of that maximum built from leave-one-out support normals.
HYPOTHESIS: A region scan statistic over calibrated log-odds maps, referenced to its leave-one-out support null distribution, raises image AUROC by at least 1 point over max-pixel scoring on BrainMRI and LiverCT (focal lesions) without loss on the other modalities, while giving test-set-invariant scores and a realised false-positive rate within 3 points of the nominal 5%.
RATIONALE: Region mass aggregates excess above a threshold but its magnitude has no reference, and log-odds fusion produces calibrated pixels but no image-level test. A scan statistic, the maximum over candidate regions of summed evidence, is the classical way to detect a localised signal of unknown position and size, and its multiple-testing problem is solved by comparing the maximum with its distribution under the null. Here the null is available from the K support normals by leave-one-out, so the image score becomes a p-value that accounts for the many candidate regions an image contains, which neither parent does.
METHOD: 1) Pixel log-odds map l(x): zero-shot branch temperature-calibrated (T on source validation), few-shot branch support z-score mapped through a source-fitted logistic; l = sum of the two log-odds (no min-max). 2) Candidate regions: connected components of {l > 0} on the 17x17 grid plus all 3x3 and 5x5 windows. 3) Scan statistic S = max over regions of sum_{x in R} l(x). 4) Null: S computed on each support normal with the bank built without it (LOO), plus 10 flipped/shifted augmentations per support, giving 11K null values. 5) p = (1 + #{S_null >= S})/(N_null + 1); score = -log10 p. 6) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) calibrated log-odds with max pixel, (ii) region mass, (iii) scan statistic with support null. Metrics: image AUROC per modality, realised FPR at p <= 0.05, score shift under resampling. Falsified if the scan statistic does not improve AUROC on BrainMRI or LiverCT or its FPR exceeds 8%.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
